title: How Secretary Grace Groner Turned Three $60 Shares Into $7 Million
alt_title_1: $180 to $7 Million: Grace Groner's 75-Year Dividend Lesson
alt_title_2: Zero Options, Zero Margin: How Three Shares Built $7 Million
description_hook: In 1935, Abbott Laboratories secretary Grace Groner bought three $60 shares of company stock ($180 total). She never used margin, never traded options, and reinvested every dividend through splits for 75 years, leaving over $7 million to Lake Forest College in 2010.

scenes.headline: Three $60 Shares Turned Into $7 Million
bullets: Bought three $60 Abbott shares in 1935 ($180 total)
Never bought another share across 75 straight years
scenes.narration: In 1935, twenty-five-year-old secretary Grace Groner bought three sixty-dollar shares of Abbott Laboratories for one hundred eighty dollars total, then held them untouched for seventy-five years.
scenes.source: Lake Forest College Bequest Announcement & Chicago Tribune (Mar 6, 2010)

scenes.headline: Zero Margin, Zero Options, 75 Years of Splits
scenes.stat_label: BEQUEATHED $7M+ TO LAKE FOREST COLLEGE AT AGE 100
bullets: Lived modestly in a tiny one-bedroom Lake Forest cottage
Reinvested every dividend through splits until January 2010
scenes.narration: Groner never traded options, never used margin debt, and lived simply in a small cottage in Lake Forest, Illinois. By reinvesting every dividend across stock splits, her three shares grew past seven million dollars by 2010.
scenes.source: Lake Forest College Bequest Announcement & Chicago Tribune (Mar 6, 2010)

scenes.headline: Overactivity Interrupts the Steep End of the Curve
scenes.left_body: Chases headlines + pays short-term taxes -> exits before year 10
scenes.right_body: Low bills + automatic dividend reinvestment -> decades of scale
scenes.narration: Most retail investors sabotage great holdings through nervous overactivity: trading macro headlines, borrowing on margin, and paying repeat tax bills right before decades of quiet dividend compounding bend steeply upward.
scenes.source: Lake Forest College Bequest Announcement & Chicago Tribune (Mar 6, 2010)

scenes.headline: Keep Fixed Bills Low and Automate Reinvestment
scenes.stat_label: UNBROKEN DECADES DO 99% OF THE HEAVY LIFTING
scenes.stat_subtext: Low burn rate + DRIP enabled + zero margin -> zero forced sales
scenes.narration: Keep fixed living bills comfortably below your income, switch on automatic dividend reinvestment, and design your cash reserves so scary recessions never force you to sell productive shares.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule based on Lake Forest College Archive (2010)

scenes.headline: Calm Endurance Beats Frantic Cleverness
scenes.stat_label: LET TIME AND DIVIDENDS MULTIPLY QUALITY ASSETS
bullets: Buy durable cash-flowing assets with money you do not need
Get out of the way while reinvested payouts compound
scenes.narration: At age one hundred, Groner gifted over seven million dollars to Lake Forest College because seventy-five years of calm endurance beat clever trading.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule based on Lake Forest College Archive (2010)
